title: Rama is born in spring
hookLine: Krishna calls spring his season, and in spring Rama is born: why Hindus throw God a birthday
carry: avatar: god takes birth among us
tomorrow: why does God catch a fever in summer?
last: AN OFFERING TO THE FIRE WITHIN.

cards: Of the seasons, I am the one that brings flowers. That's Krishna in the Bhagavad Gita, paraphrased, naming the places his glory shows, and among the seasons he picks spring.
Ayurveda's Charaka reads the same season more plainly: winter's heaviness thaws, so eat lighter and move more. But Hindus remember spring for something bigger.
In the spring month of Chaitra, in Ayodhya, an old king who waited years for a child finally hears a baby cry. Today, spring, and the birth of Rama.

teach.b: The story is in Valmiki's Ramayana. King Dasharatha has everything but a son, and he grows old waiting. So he holds a great fire sacrifice.
Out of the fire, the poem says, rises a shining being carrying a golden vessel of payasa, sweet rice cooked in milk, a gift from the gods, and Dasharatha shares it among his three queens.
Meanwhile the gods have a problem.
The demon king Ravana is protected by a boon: no god or demon can kill him. He never thought to ask for safety from a human. So Vishnu agrees to be born as one.
And in Chaitra, on the ninth day of the bright half of the month, Queen Kausalya gives birth to Rama.
Here's the teaching, plainly: avatar, God coming down. Hindus believe God takes birth in the world, again and again, when it needs setting right.

Krishna says it in the Gita, paraphrased: whenever dharma falls and wrong rises, I come into being, age after age. And notice how Rama arrives. Not as a blaze in the sky, but as a baby who has to be fed and held.

teach.h: RAMA NAVAMI: A CRADLE AT MIDDAY
teach.b: So every spring Hindus keep Rama Navami, the ninth. Many temples mark the birth around midday, rock a small cradle, sing and share sweets.
A birthday party for God sounds strange until you see the point: God came close enough to be born into a family.

how: On Rama Navami, in the spring month of Chaitra, many Hindu temples and homes mark Rama's birth around midday with a cradle, songs and sweets, and many devotees keep a fast; people who follow Ayurveda also eat lighter and move more as the spring thaw begins.

games.why: Ravana never asked for safety from humans, so Vishnu is born as Rama. that is avatar: God coming down, all the way to a cradle.

practice: Sit tall and let three slow breaths come and go. Then picture something newly born in your life this season, a plant, a plan, a baby in the family, and hold it in mind the way you'd hold an infant: gently, with both hands.
If you pray, say Rama's name softly a few times, as many Hindus do. If you don't, simply rest in the welcome.

wordCard.voice: The seasons. In spring, Charaka's thaw and the Gita's flowers, and the Hindu year's great spring birth: Rama, God born as a child in the month of Chaitra. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: avatara, a coming down. The Hindu word for God taking birth in the world, as Rama and as Krishna.

carryVoice: Your line: avatar, God takes birth among us. That's why Rama Navami is a birthday. See you tomorrow.
